light step for Yama's abode in order to acquaint him with what 
had taken place and there he found the God Yama before a fire, 
desling out justice to every being according to his deserts. 
" Then Yama, becoming aware of the presence of that great 
Rishi Narada, offering him a comfortable seat and the Arghya, 
according to tradition, said to him :-
" ' 0 Devarishi, is all well or is righteousness in jeopardy ? 
Wherefore hast thou come hither, thou who art revered by the 
Gods and Gandharvas ? ' 
" Thereupon Narada, that blessed Rishi, answered him

fitting ! That ranger of the night, named Dashagriva, is coming 
here to overthrow thee by the force of his will, though thou art 
invincible. It is on this account that I have come hither in all 
haste, fearing what would befall thee, 0 Lord Who bearest the 
Rod.''

brief.summary_1line: Ravana invades Yama’s realm, witnesses hell’s punishments and rewards, frees the damned, and battles Yama’s armies with devastating celestial weapons.

image_candidates.scene_text: Ravana’s radiant Pushpaka chariot blazes like the sun as it descends into the dark realm of Yama, illuminating the land of the dead.
The Vaitarani river of blood where tormented souls struggle through burning sand while worms and dogs devour the damned on the banks.
Ravana stands blood-soaked on the battlefield, drawing the flaming Pashupata missile as Yama’s vast army surrounds him like storm clouds.
